validity.researcher_notes: This is a real, correctly-classified GASCO national-grid gas TRANSMISSION trunk (not gathering/plant-internal), distinct from any of the other 29 Egypt operating-gas rows in the roster. Existence/specs corroborated by three genuinely independent origins: (1) Egyptian government (presidency.eg official project page, republished verbatim by egy-map.com [which explicitly cites 'Official website of the Egyptian Presidency' as its source] and by petro-news.com's ministry-sourced '39 مشروعاً' project list -- these three all trace to ONE underlying government announcement, so treated as a single origin for tiering purposes) -- all agree: 42-inch diameter, 165 km total length, cost EGP 3.335 billion (matches GEM's SegmentCost of 3,335,000,000 EGP exactly), governorates Cairo/Ismailia/Port Said, completed July 2019, purpose = strengthen national gas grid + feed the New Administrative Capital power station + support south-Cairo/Upper Egypt consumers. (2) Petrojet (the EPC contractor) publishes its own project portfolio entry titled 'El Tina-new capital (42"-165 KM)', independently confirming the exact same diameter+length and giving a 2-phase breakdown: Phase 1 El-Tina -> Abu Sultan, 92 km (23 HDD crossings); Phase 2 Abu Sultan -> Hot Tap of Dahshour Pipeline at the New Capital, 73 km (11 HDD crossings) -- 92+73=165, consistent with GEM's LengthKnown=165. (3) The Energy Year (industry trade journal, quoting GASCO chairman Yasser Salah El Din) independently names 'the Al-Tina - Abu-Sultan - New Administrative Capital pipeline to transport gas produced in the Zohr field to feed the power station of the New Administrative Capital' as a 2018-era GASCO project -- consistent corridor and purpose, written independently of the government press release. IMPORTANT CAVEAT AVOIDED: an EIB-published Environmental Impact Assessment PDF (petrosafe/GASCO, dated October 2005) also covers a project literally named 'El Tina - Abu Sultan Onshore Gas Pipeline' -- but that document describes a DIFFERENT, older, 32-inch/60 km pipeline (purpose: feed Ataqa power station + support the Oyoun Mossa pipeline; unrelated to the New Administrative Capital, which did not exist as a concept until c.2015). I confirmed this is NOT the same asset as P3366 (name reuse of the El Tina/Abu Sultan corridor for two different vintages of pipeline) and did not use it as a source for this row's specs or coordinates. Checked against the full 30-row Egypt-operating-gas roster and the GulfPub roster for a duplicate/relabel: no match -- P3343 'El Tina Gas Pipeline' (El Tina -> Al Qalyubia, 170 km, 42in) sounded like a possible duplicate given the shared 'El Tina' origin and diameter, but independent Arabic-language search surfaced it as a distinct GASCO project ('doubling/twinning of the El Tina West/Mit Nama line', 168 km, feeding Zohr-area gas south to support the national grid generally) with a different destination (Mit Nama/Qalyubia, north of Cairo, vs. Abu Sultan/New Capital, east of Cairo) and different official description -- not the same physical pipe as P3366. No GulfPub Egypt gas record matches this corridor either. url_verifier could not machine-verify the Petrojet page (Angular SPA with no server-rendered body text) or The Energy Year article (Cloudflare-blocked, HTTP 403), so those two independent corroborators are documented here for the human record but are NOT included in proposed_refs; only egy-map.com and petro-news.com (both HTTP 200 + '165' content-verified) are proposed as citable refs.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM (both the sheet and the gem.wiki infobox) lists Owner1 = Operator = Parent company = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding company' (EGAS) at 100%. EGAS is Egypt's upstream state holding company; it is not itself the entity that builds/runs high-pressure gas TRANSMISSION trunk pipelines -- that role belongs to GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company), a wholly EGAS-owned subsidiary. Independent trade-press corroboration: The Energy Year's profile of GASCO's chairman (Yasser Salah El Din) states plainly that 'GASCO implemented ... the Al-Tina - Abu-Sultan - New Administrative Capital pipeline' as one of GASCO's projects. This is consistent with the broader pattern for Egypt's national gas grid (GASCO is the designated builder/operator of virtually all such trunk lines; e.g., the EIB-published 2005 EIA for the older, unrelated 'El Tina-Abu Sultan' 32in/60km line was likewise issued on GASCO letterhead as 'Egyptian Natural Gas Co. (GASCO)'). I could not find a source that names EGAS specifically as the constructing/operating entity for this pipeline -- EGAS's role here looks like the standard ultimate-holding-company attribution, not a documented operational one. Could not verify with a second independent, url_verifier-passing source (The Energy Year is Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch; Petrojet's own contractor page, which would also help, is a JS-rendered SPA with no server-side text to verify), so this stays a flagged concern for human review rather than a corrected value. Owner% of 100% for a single owner is otherwise internally consistent.

routes.start_name: El Tina / Qantara East area, Port Said Governorate (GASCO gas junction on the Suez Canal's east bank, near the Tina Plain)
routes.end_name: New Administrative Capital power station area, east of Cairo (Phase 2 ties into the 'Hot Tap of Dahshour Pipeline' at the New Capital)

waypoints.name: Abu Sultan, Ismailia Governorate (phase boundary: 92 km from El Tina; 73 km on to the New Capital tie-in per Petrojet's own project breakdown)

routes.corridor_desc: Two-phase GASCO trunk built by Petrojet: Phase 1 runs ~92 km from a valve/tie-in point at El Tina (on the Suez Canal's east bank in Port Said Governorate, in the Tina Plain / Qantara East area) south through Ismailia Governorate to Abu Sultan (23 HDD crossings along the way, per Petrojet). Phase 2 continues ~73 km from Abu Sultan west/southwest to a hot-tap tie-in with the existing Dahshour Pipeline at the New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo (11 HDD crossings). Total 165 km across Port Said, Ismailia, and Cairo governorates -- note GEM's own Location fields only record Port Said (start) and Cairo (end) and omit the Ismailia governorate the line actually transits via Abu Sultan. I have HIGH confidence in this waypoint order and the 92km/73km split (Petrojet, the constructing contractor) and in the 3 governorates (government source + Petrojet), but LOW confidence in precise point coordinates: I did NOT use the specific valve-room coordinates in an EIB/PETROSAFE 2005 EIA document that also covers an 'El Tina-Abu Sultan' corridor, because that document is for a different, older (32in/60km, Ataqa-power-station-feed) pipeline, not this one -- reusing its coordinates here would misattribute a different asset's surveyed route to P3366. The single coordinate I did supply (New Administrative Capital, ~30.02N/31.74E) is general public-geography knowledge of the New Capital's location east of Cairo, not sourced from a pipeline-specific document -- treat as a loose bound, not a surveyed point. El Tina and Abu Sultan are left uncoordinated (null) rather than guessed.
routes.researcher_notes: Waypoint order and km split from Petrojet's own (non-citable, JS-rendered) project page; governorates from the citable government-sourced cluster. No coordinates fabricated -- New Capital point is loose public-geography knowledge, El Tina/Abu Sultan left null. A human routes-repo pass should locate the actual GASCO valve rooms/hot-tap point via satellite imagery or a GASCO GIS source before any route is added.

summary: P3366 confirmed real and correctly classified (GASCO 42in/165km national-grid trunk built 2018-2019 by Petrojet to feed the New Administrative Capital power station with Zohr-field gas); specs/dates/cost corroborated, no duplicate found (checked vs P3343/roster/GulfPub). One attribution concern staged: Owner/Operator recorded as EGAS but independent trade press attributes construction/operation to GASCO. Route: proposed medium-confidence corridor (El Tina -> Abu Sultan -> New Capital/Dahshour hot-tap) with one loose coordinate; no UNRESOLVED fills (Capacity left blank, no verifiable number found).
